QS.question: Explain cohesion and coupling, and why high cohesion and low coupling are desirable.
QS.solution: Cohesion measures how strongly the responsibilities inside a module belong together. Coupling measures dependency between modules. Prefer a focused module such as TaxCalculator and narrow data contracts. Passing order totals is data coupling; passing an entire Order object for a single field is stamp coupling; mode flags can create control coupling; shared globals create common coupling; changing another module’s internals is content coupling. A cohesive billing module changes for billing rules, while a stable invoice interface protects other modules from that change. Low coupling does not imply zero collaboration.

QS.solution: A quality product satisfies explicit requirements and real user needs, behaves correctly and reliably, is usable and secure, and can be maintained and tested. QS.question: Explain Scrum roles, artifacts, backlog differences, and late change handling.

Select a process by the uncertainty

Stable requirements fit a staged process with feedback to earlier phases. Use prototyping to learn a workflow, Spiral for substantial risks, RAD for modular time-boxed delivery, and Scrum when stakeholder feedback can regularly redirect product work. Artifacts: Product Backlog (Product Goal), Sprint Backlog (Sprint Goal), and Increment (Definition of Done).

NOTES.html:
Cohesion, coupling and design choices

Cohesion measures how strongly the responsibilities inside a module belong together. Coupling measures dependency between modules. Prefer a focused module such as TaxCalculator and narrow data contracts. Passing order totals is data coupling; passing an entire Order object for a single field is stamp coupling; mode flags can create control coupling; shared globals create common coupling; changing another module’s internals is content coupling. From weakest to strongest in a common textbook ordering: coincidental (miscellaneous utilities), logical (all input operations selected by a flag), temporal (startup tasks), procedural (steps grouped by order), communicational (operate on the same record), sequential (output of one step feeds the next), functional (one well-defined operation).

NOTES.html:
Build tests from rules and paths

Black-box testing derives tests from requirements. Equivalence partitioning selects representatives of valid and invalid classes; boundary-value analysis tests at and just around limits; decision tables cover rule combinations. White-box testing derives tests from implementation structure: statements, branches, conditions, basis paths, and data-flow or loop behavior. For a single connected CFG, V(G)=E−N+2. For binary decisions it also equals number of predicates plus one. A k-way branch contributes k−1.

NOTES.html:
Quality, process maturity and reliability

A quality product satisfies explicit requirements and real user needs, behaves correctly and reliably, is usable and secure, and can be maintained and tested. Product assurance inspects and tests the delivered product; process assurance also builds prevention into standards, reviews, measurement, corrective action, and continuous improvement. Both remain necessary. Reliability is probability of failure-free operation under a specified profile and duration. Availability also depends on recovery time.

NOTES.html:
Maintain and modernize a system

Maintain software as requirements and its environment change. Classify the work as corrective, adaptive, perfective or preventive. SCM controls versions and baselines. Reverse engineering analyzes an existing system to recover its design, data model, and requirements without changing its behavior. Re-engineering uses that understanding to improve the implementation through restructuring, data migration, documentation and forward engineering, checked against regression tests.
